questions.q: Why does this fraud detection system have no sensible batch processing path?
options: Fraud detection systems never need to process data quickly
This system doesn't actually process any transaction data
Batch processing is always faster than streaming for fraud detection
A transaction has to be scored before it completes, not after, so a delayed batch score is useless
questions.explain: The whole point is to act before the transaction completes, which rules out any "score it later" batch path.

questions.q: Why does the scoring write need to be idempotent, keyed on transaction_id?
options: Idempotent writes always run slower than non-idempotent ones
Because a duplicated event delivery could otherwise score a transaction twice or flag a duplicate as separate fraud
Idempotency has no relevance to a fraud detection system
Transaction IDs are only used for billing, not scoring
questions.explain: The MERGE pattern makes scoring the same transaction_id twice a no-op instead of producing a second, misleading signal.

questions.q: Why does this system deliberately lean AP rather than CP, per the CAP analysis from Lesson 19?
options: AP systems are always more secure against fraud than CP systems
Refusing to score during a partition just because a feature might be slightly stale would block legitimate purchases for no real benefit
CP would make the system faster, so it was rejected for being too fast
This system has no relationship to the CAP theorem at all
questions.explain: Scoring against slightly stale rolling features is preferable to erroring out and blocking a real transaction.

questions.q: What role does Fabric's Activator play in this design?
options: Activator is responsible for ingesting the raw transaction events
Activator computes the rolling features used in scoring
It turns a crossed fraud-score threshold into an actual real-time alert, rather than leaving the flagged score sitting unused in a table
Activator has no role in this system's design
questions.explain: A flagged score is only useful once something acts on it — Activator is the concrete answer to "then what."

questions.q: Why do watermarks matter for the rolling feature computation in this pipeline?
options: Watermarks eliminate the need for idempotent scoring
Watermarks are only relevant to batch processing, never streaming
They handle events that arrive late, which affects time-windowed features like "spend in the last 5 minutes"
Watermarks have no connection to feature computation
questions.explain: Late-arriving events need to be handled correctly for a rolling, time-windowed feature to be accurate.
